applicable_when: The kernel uses ALLOW_TF32=False, forcing the FP32 FFMA path through the FMA pipeline. This path requires 255 registers per thread — the hardware maximum — which limits the block count to only 2 blocks/SM (Block Limit Registers = 2) and theoretical occupancy to 12.5%. With only 1.96 active warps/scheduler and 58.5% of cycles having no eligible warp, the GPU is severely latency-bound due to insufficient warp-level parallelism. Enabling allow_tf32=True in tl.dot switches the dot-product accumulation to Tensor Core MMA instructions, which dramatically reduce register pressure, deliver ~8x the throughput of FP32 FFMA, and allow more blocks/SM to be resident simultaneously.

applicable_when: The kernel uses BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=32 with only 128 threads per block. This 128x128 accumulator tile requires each thread to hold 128 FP32 accumulator values plus tile data in registers, driving register usage to 255/thread — the hardware maximum. This caps occupancy at 12.5% (2 blocks/SM due to register limit), leaving schedulers idle 58.5% of cycles. Reducing tile sizes (e.g., BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64 or BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=64) dramatically cuts per-thread register demand, allowing more blocks per SM and hiding latency. Additionally, B's stride layout (stride_bk=1, stride_bn=1024) with order=(1,0) causes 5.3-way shared memory bank conflicts; changing BLOCK_K or adjusting num_warps can improve bank access patterns. Adding @triton.autotune lets the runtime find the optimal configuration across these axes.
